The *Aṅkurapetavatthu* (Pv 21), rendered in English as *The Merchant Aṅkura*, is a narrative text belonging to the *Petavatthu* collection. Its core theme centers on the principle that acts of giving (*dāna*) unfailingly yield positive karmic fruit. The narrative traditions regarding Aṅkura are prominently connected to multiple canonical suttas and stories throughout the Pali canon, being cited or referenced in the *Chaḷaṅgadānasutta* (AN 6.37), the *Sādhusutta* (SN 1.33), and numerous Jātaka tales, including the *Ādittajātaka* (Ja 424), *Akittijātaka* (Ja 480), *Mahāvāṇijajātaka* (Ja 493), and the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547).
